notes.emailHon: In business writing, -(으)시- honors the reader's actions, while -드리- forms humble verbs for your own actions toward them.
notes.emailWord: Business email vocabulary is mostly Sino-Korean nouns; look-alike nouns can differ sharply in meaning.

notes.phoneHon: On the phone, use 계시다 (not 있다) for the person you ask for, and humble -드리- verbs for your own actions toward the caller.

entries.ko: 저희는 장기 계약을 전제로 가격을 제안드립니다.
entries.g: We are proposing this price on the premise of a long-term contract.

entries.ko: 귀사의 제안은 매력적이지만 예산상 어려움이 있습니다.
entries.g: Your company's proposal is attractive, but we have difficulty with the budget.

entries.ko: 양보할 수 있는 부분과 그렇지 않은 부분이 있습니다.
entries.g: There are parts we can concede and parts we cannot.

entries.ko: 서로 한 걸음씩 물러서면 합의점을 찾을 수 있을 것입니다.
entries.g: If each of us steps back a little, we will be able to find common ground.
We must also consider the other party's position thoroughly.

entries.ko:
A: 단가를 조금 조정해 주실 수 있겠습니까?
B: 대량 주문이라면 5% 할인해 드릴 수 있습니다.
A: 감사합니다. 납기는 어떻게 됩니까?
B: 주문 후 2주 안에 납품하겠습니다.
entries.g:
A: Could you adjust the unit price a little?
B: If it is a bulk order, I can give you a 5 percent discount.
A: Thank you. What about the delivery date?
B: We will deliver within two weeks after the order.

read.true: B는 대량 주문이면 5% 할인할 수 있다고 했습니다.
false: 납품은 두 달 안에 하기로 했습니다.

notes.etHon: Never attach 님 or 께서 to your own name or title when introducing yourself; use them for the other person's title and actions.
notes.etTitle: Korean workplace ranks run roughly 사원, 대리, 과장, 차장, 부장, 이사, and people are addressed by title plus 님.

entries.g: business card
job title
staff member; junior employee
assistant manager
manager (section chief)
deputy general manager
director (executive)
client's contact person
to exchange greetings
It is a pleasure to meet you.
entries.s: You are meeting a business contact for the first time.

entries.g: I look forward to working with you.
entries.s: You ask for a good working relationship after being introduced.

entries.g: Let me introduce myself first.
entries.s: You begin a first meeting by introducing yourself.

entries.g: May I have one of your business cards?
entries.s: You politely ask a new contact for a card.

entries.g: I have heard a lot about you.
entries.s: You meet someone you already know of by reputation.

entries.ko: 명함은 두 손으로 공손히 건네는 것이 예의입니다.
entries.g: It is good manners to hand over a business card politely with both hands.
I am Assistant Manager Lee Min-ho of the Sales Team at Hanbit Trading.
Manager Park will be here shortly.
Department Manager, could you check this document?
President, a guest from a client company has arrived.

entries.ko: 윗사람은 이름 대신 직함으로 부르는 것이 예의입니다.
entries.g: It is polite to address a senior by job title instead of by name.

cloze.blank: 윗사람은 이름 대신 ____ 부르는 것이 예의입니다.

entries.ko: 처음 만난 거래처에는 존댓말을 사용해야 합니다.
entries.g: You must use honorific speech with a client you have just met.
I will show you to the meeting room.
I will write my contact details on the back of my card.

entries.ko: 상대방의 직함을 잘못 부르면 실례가 됩니다.
entries.g: Calling someone by the wrong title is rude.

entries.ko:
A: 처음 뵙겠습니다. 한빛상사 이지은 대리입니다.
B: 안녕하십니까? 서울물산 최영수 과장입니다. 명함 여기 있습니다.
A: 감사합니다. 저도 명함 드리겠습니다.
B: 앞으로 잘 부탁드립니다.
entries.g:
A: Nice to meet you. I am Assistant Manager Lee Ji-eun of Hanbit Trading.
B: Hello. I am Manager Choi Young-su of Seoul Trading. Here is my card.
A: Thank you. Let me give you my card too.
B: I look forward to working with you.

entries.ko:
A: 부장님, 서울물산 최 과장님이 오셨습니다.
B: 응접실로 모셔 주세요.
A: 네, 안내해 드리겠습니다.
B: 차도 한 잔 부탁합니다.
entries.g:
A: Department Manager, Manager Choi from Seoul Trading has arrived.
B: Please show him to the reception room.
A: Yes, I will guide him.
B: Please also bring a cup of tea.

notes.revHon: Review: -(으)시- honors the other person, humble -드리- verbs describe your own actions toward them, and -(스)ㅂ니다 keeps the tone formal.
notes.revVocab: Review: business Sino-Korean nouns often look alike, so choose by meaning and by the verb they combine with.

entries.g: approval (signing off on a document)
business trip
overtime work at night
client; business partner company
division of work
working from home
meeting materials
Let me check the meeting schedule for a moment.
entries.s: Someone asks for a meeting time and you need to look at your calendar.

entries.g: Sorry, but could you explain once more?
entries.s: You did not follow an explanation and politely ask for it again.

entries.g: Thank you for your help.
entries.s: A colleague has helped you finish your work.

entries.g: I will send it to you by the end of today.
entries.s: You promise a client to deliver a document by the end of the day.

entries.g: Please go ahead and speak first.
entries.s: You politely let a guest begin speaking in a meeting.

entries.ko: 출장 보고서는 다녀온 후 일주일 이내에 제출해야 합니다.
entries.g: The business trip report must be submitted within a week after returning.

cloze.blank: 출장 보고서는 다녀온 후 일주일 이내에 ____ 합니다.

entries.ko: 이 건은 부장님의 결재를 받은 후에 진행하겠습니다.
entries.g: I will proceed with this matter after getting the department manager's approval.

cloze.blank: 이 건은 부장님의 결재를 ____ 후에 진행하겠습니다.

entries.ko: 제가 담당하고 있는 업무는 거래처 관리입니다.
entries.g: The work I am in charge of is managing client accounts.

entries.ko: 이번 주는 업무가 많아서 야근을 해야 할 것 같습니다.
entries.g: I have a lot of work this week, so I think I will have to work overtime.
You can reach me by messenger even while I work from home.

entries.ko: 급한 일이 생겨서 회의에 참석하지 못할 것 같습니다.
entries.g: Something urgent came up, so I do not think I can attend the meeting.

cloze.blank: 급한 일이 생겨서 회의에 ____ 못할 것 같습니다.

entries.g: I will contact you after reporting to the department manager.
This quarter's sales exceeded the target by 10 percent.

entries.ko: 계약서에 서명하기 전에 조건을 다시 확인해 주십시오.
entries.g: Please check the terms again before signing the contract.

cloze.blank: 계약서에 서명하기 ____ 조건을 다시 확인해 주십시오.

entries.ko: 신제품 반응이 좋아서 주문이 두 배로 늘었습니다.
entries.g: The new product was well received, so orders doubled.
I sent the quotation to the customer.
I forgot to attach the file to the email.

entries.ko:
A: 대리님, 내일 출장 일정을 확인해 주시겠습니까?
B: 네, 오전 아홉 시 비행기로 부산에 가십니다.
A: 거래처 미팅은 몇 시입니까?
B: 오후 두 시이고, 회의 자료는 메일로 보내 드렸습니다.
entries.g:
A: Assistant Manager, could you check tomorrow's business trip schedule?
B: Yes, you are going to Busan on a flight at nine in the morning.
A: What time is the client meeting?
B: It is at two in the afternoon, and I have emailed you the meeting materials.

entries.ko:
이 부장님께,
결재 요청드립니다.
신규 거래처와의 계약서를 첨부하였으니 검토해 주시기 바랍니다.
오늘 중으로 회신해 주시면 감사하겠습니다.
entries.g:
To Department Manager Lee,
I am requesting your approval.
I have attached the contract with the new client, so please review it.
I would appreciate it if you could reply within today.
